approved_text: Is it true that, as n → ∞ over natural numbers, the sum of 1/p over all primes p ≤ n for which the remainder n mod p is greater than p/2 is asymptotic to (log log n)/2, i.e. their ratio tends to 1?
draft: Is it true that, as n → ∞ over natural numbers, the sum of 1/p over all primes p ≤ n for which the remainder n mod p is greater than p/2 is asymptotic to (log log n)/2, i.e. their ratio tends to 1?
source_docstrings:
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

A conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].

By $n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}$ we mean $n\equiv r\pmod{p}$ for some integer $r$ with $p/2<r<p$.
source_lean:
theorem erdos_726 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter
          (fun p : ℕ ↦ p.Prime ∧ (p : ℝ) / 2 < (n % p : ℝ)),
        (1 : ℝ) / (p : ℝ))
      ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) / 2)
